summary: What this demonstration claims, and what it deliberately does not. The boundary is checked-in data so it cannot drift silently.

claimed.title: Uncontrolled Search Path Element
claimed.why: A fixed search path contains an element an untrusted publisher can write to, and the entry names package-manager dependency confusion directly. Its ALLOWED-WITH-REVIEW mapping note is preserved rather than hidden.

claimed.title: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
claimed.why: The vulnerable build incorporates functionality from an untrusted control sphere. It complements the more precise CWE-427 rather than replacing it.

claimed.title: Software and Data Integrity Failures
claimed.why: OWASP describes applications consuming libraries or modules from untrusted repositories and tells package managers to consume trusted repositories.

claimed.title: Supply Chain
claimed.why: The affected consumer is an LLM release pipeline, and a third-party software dependency changes whether a model candidate is approved.

not_claimed.title: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
not_claimed.why: No component here is vulnerable, outdated, deprecated or unmaintained, and no maintenance state affects selection. OWASP's own A06 guidance sends modified or malicious package provenance to A08.

not_claimed.title: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
not_claimed.why: Reliance on an unmaintained component is not the behaviour demonstrated here. Claiming it would fill a coverage square while teaching a different root cause.

not_claimed.title: Data and Model Poisoning
not_claimed.why: Model candidates, their classifications and every evaluation input are byte-identical between runs. Only the resolved software artifact changes.

no_real_package_manager_claim: The resolver here is a documented package-manager-agnostic model. No assertion is made that npm, pip, Maven, NuGet, Go modules, Cargo, RubyGems or any other named tool follows this project's precedence or tie rule.
